_wilmslowPiccolinoCiboSource: Piccolino Grande and Cibo Gran Cafe added 2026-09-18 at explicit user request (named directly: 'piccolino's gran cafe, cibo gran cafe' — the user knows both personally). Both are exactly the case the two-gate model (CLAUDE.md Hard rule 1, 2026-09-16) was built for: real multi-site groups that the old single chain-veto would have excluded outright, now judged on Gate 1/Gate 2 instead. Piccolino Grande, 6-12 Swan Street (postcode SK9 1HE, geocoded via postcodes.io) is part of the national Piccolino chain (Individual Restaurants) — verified via piccolinorestaurants.com, confidentials.com and themanc.com as a GBP 2m, 2026 rebuild described as Piccolino's most ambitious site outside London (marble/brass/terrazzo interior, copper-clad pizza oven, a winterised Tuscan terrace, a tableside 'carbonara grande' and Fassona Piedmontese T-bone). Gate 1: passes cleanly — an upscale, well-regarded premium-casual group, not mass-market high-street. Gate 2 distinctiveness: 3 — CLAUDE.md's own worked example ('a good Piccolino') is this exact case; the flagship-tier rebuild argues for the top of that band rather than a generic 3, but the format is still a familiar national brand, not singular. ownership='group'. Cibo Gran Cafe, 31-33 Grove Arcade (postcode SK9 1DU) is the newer sibling site to the already-seeded Cibo (26-28 Green Lane, two minutes away) — verified via ciborestaurants.co.uk and squaremeal.co.uk as a combined bar/ristorante/artisanal-patisserie format with private event space (90 seated/150 standing) and a Sunday afternoon tea. Researching this site surfaced that Cibo Restaurants is a real 5-site regional group (Manchester, Hale, two Wilmslow sites, Disley), not the single independent restaurant the existing Cibo entry's ownership defaulted to under migration 0009's blanket backfill (distinctiveness=4/ownership='independent' applied to all 244 pre-existing rows) — that default is corrected alongside this addition (ownership -> 'small_group') rather than left silently wrong now that real research contradicts it. Cibo Gran Cafe Gate 1: passes (same small regional group, same quality bar). Gate 2 distinctiveness: 3 — a genuinely less common combined format for the area, but still a recognisable extension of an existing local brand rather than a singular find. ownership='small_group'. Both venues' dietary tags (vegetarian/vegan/gluten-free) are sourced, not assumed: Piccolino's own allergen pages confirm gluten-free pasta and vegan substitutions on request; Cibo Gran Cafe's listings confirm vegetarian/vegan/gluten-free options (though guest feedback on gluten-free handling there is mixed — flagged, not hidden). BRUNCH SPOT (already used for Caramello) reused for Cibo Gran Cafe rather than inventing a new type, since its daytime cafe/patisserie identity fits that tile cleanly. Distinctiveness/ownership values here are documented in this note and applied directly via SQL (supabase/migrations/0013_wilmslow_piccolino_cibo.sql) — not stored as JSON fields on the venue entries below, since no other entry in this file carries those fields yet and adding them to only two would make the schema inconsistent; the live database is the real source of truth for those two columns going forward (see 0010_growth_engine.sql's own source-of-truth-flip note). One more thing surfaced re-reading _wilmslowDensitySource below: its chain-exclusion list from the original August pass (Slug & Lettuce, Revolution, The Botanist, Unico Lounge/The Lounges, Anthology/Greene King, The King William/Robinsons, Stanneylands/JW Lees) is the same kind of list that produced the Mouro Coffee Bar re-evaluation candidate elsewhere — worth a fresh Gate 1/Gate 2 pass, not done as part of this addition.
_source: Transcribed from the Claude Design handoff bundle's VENUES constant in Curia.dc.html (fetched 2026-07-30) — real illustrative seed venues, not chains, matching Hard rule 1. `reason` strings are the actual brand-voice match-reason copy from the prototype; use as the register/quality bar for new copy, not verbatim filler. Added by curia-moments-journeys (M6): The Old Cellars is transcribed from the prototype's own VENUES constant (this file was previously a 15-of-18 subset that happened to omit it, even though the prototype's own moments picks reference it by name). Everyman Cinema/Rudy's/Porta are transcribed from the prototype's own JOURNEYS constant (the 'Date Night in Altrincham' stops, which carry name/kind/note there but were never given a standalone VENUES entry in the prototype) — lat/lon/spend/base/bands for those three are new, plausible fill-ins (Altrincham town centre) rather than transcribed, since the prototype never assigned them any.
_metroScopeNote: A Los Angeles metro (Beverly Hills, West Hollywood, Santa Monica, Venice, Culver City — 31 real, independently-verified venues) existed here from an earlier 2026-08 pass and was removed at explicit later request (2026-08) to keep the app scoped to Manchester/Cheshire only. See docs/data/districts.json's own _metroScopeNote for the same removal on the district side.
_santoriniVenueSource: 2026-09, at explicit user request: a friend of the user's is in Santorini right now wanting to test the app, which had no coverage there at all — 52 real venues added across the four new Santorini districts (see docs/data/districts.json's own _santoriniSource note), researched via five parallel independent web-search passes (beach clubs; Fira nightlife; Oia/Imerovigli sunset bars & wineries; shopping & activities, prioritised per explicit user direction; restaurants) rather than one broad sweep, each instructed to skip any business it couldn't independently confirm as real and currently operating rather than guess. Landed at 7 beach clubs (target: at least 5), 8 late-night venues i.e. genuinely open past midnight (target: at least 5), 13 Do venues with shopping as the clear majority (10 of 13 are boutiques/galleries/a pottery studio, matching the explicit 'prioritize shopping' direction) and 15 Eat venues spread across all four districts. Drink landed at 17 real venues against a 20 target — an honest shortfall from real-research constraints, not padded to round out the number (the same 'honest number, not a padded one' discipline as the 2026-08 Wilmslow Drink pass and 2026-09-03 Prestbury/Cheadle Hulme pass elsewhere in this file). Three real, verified wineries the research turned up (Santo Wines/Pyrgos, Venetsanos Winery/Megalochori, Art Space Winery/Exo Gonia) and one real, verified archaeological site (Akrotiri Archaeological Site/Akrotiri village) were deliberately excluded rather than misattributed to one of the four chosen districts — all four sit in other real Santorini villages several kilometres from Oia/Fira/Imerovigli/Perissa-Perivolos, and this file's location data is load-bearing (distance is a hard filter per CLAUDE.md's Matchmaking contract), so a wrong district would be a real accuracy bug, not a rounding error; a fifth real Domaine Sigalas listing from the shopping/activities pass was a duplicate of the same venue already added from the wineries pass and was dropped rather than double-counted. Coordinates: Greece has no UK-style postcode API, so geocoding used Nominatim (OpenStreetMap's free geocoder, 1 req/sec rate-limited per its usage policy) with each venue's real found address as the query; roughly half resolved to a precise point, the rest fell back to their real village/beach-area centroid (e.g. Perivolos beach's own OSM polygon centroid) with small manual spread within that area's real bounding box so venues on the same beach or caldera strip don't stack on one exact pixel — an honest area-level approximation, not a fabricated precise address, matching this file's own established 'skip rather than guess' standard applied to location precision instead of venue identity. Introduces 12 new venue types (NIGHTCLUB, SPORTS BAR, SUNSET BAR, WINERY, JEWELLERY BOUTIQUE, FASHION BOUTIQUE, MUSEUM, BOAT TOUR, SOUVLAKI SPOT, SEAFOOD RESTAURANT, plus reuse of existing JAZZ BAR/CHAMPAGNE BAR/WINE BAR/GREEK TAVERNA/FINE DINING/BRUNCH SPOT/BAKERY/POTTERY STUDIO/COOKERY SCHOOL/ART GALLERY types where a real fit existed) — all mapped in src/lib/scoring/tile-catalog-map.ts's CATEGORY_BY_VENUE_TYPE; BEACH CLUB is the only one with a dedicated onboarding tile ('Beach clubs', the new Holiday category), the rest are category-only for now, same treatment as this file's many existing category-only UK venue types. petFriendly defaulted false and dietaryOptions defaulted ['none'] for every venue except where a source explicitly confirmed otherwise (En Lefko and Tranquilo: vegan-friendly kitchens; Domaine Sigalas: a winery tasting has no meat/dairy to exclude; Avocado Restaurant: explicitly confirmed real vegetarian options; Greek Cooking Class with Areti: vegetarian-inclusive per its own listing) — same conservative-default rule as every dietary/pet pass elsewhere in this file, not inferred from venue type alone.
_santoriniCoordinateCorrectionSource: 2026-09, at explicit user report ('some venues are showing as in the ocean'): confirmed real via a proper point-in-polygon check, not just eyeballing — fetched Santorini/Thira's actual landmass polygon from Nominatim (polygon_geojson=1) and tested every one of the 52 Santorini venues plus all 4 district centroids against it programmatically (sanity-checked first against a known mid-caldera water point and a known-good Fira land point, both resolved correctly). 10 venues and the Imerovigli district centroid itself were genuinely off the island polygon, into the caldera or a harbour/marina's water area: Astra Suites Pool Bar, Buddha-Bar Beach Sunset Lounge and Sand Lily Boutique (all three, plus the Imerovigli district row, shared one bad hand-picked 'Imerovigli centroid' coordinate that was never actually verified against a real geocode — turned out to sit in the caldera, ~600m from Imerovigli's real village centre); The Athenian House and Kapari Wine Restaurant used the same bad point with a small offset, same root cause; Lioyerma Lounge Cafe Pool Bar and Sunset Oia Sailing Cruises both geocoded to Ammoudi Bay's harbour/water area rather than the shoreline buildings; To Psaraki geocoded to Vlychada Marina's water rather than the restaurant on its edge; Theros Wave Bar's 'Eros Beach, Vlychada' geocode landed offshore; Chilli Beach Bar's hand-picked Perivolos-beach offset landed just past the sand. Fixed by nudging each in small steps from its original point toward a real, independently-confirmed on-land anchor nearby (the real Imerovigli village centroid for the five Imerovigli venues plus the district row itself; Oia's village centre for the two Ammoudi venues; each area's already-verified beach/marina land point for the rest), stopping at the smallest shift that lands on the actual polygon — movement ranged 37-590m, not a wholesale re-geocode. Re-ran the same point-in-polygon check against all 52 venues and all 4 district centroids afterward: zero flagged. The other 42 venues' coordinates were confirmed correct by this same check, not just left alone on the assumption they were fine.
_londonVenueSource: 2026-09-15, at explicit user request: first venues for London's 6 new districts (see docs/data/districts.json's own _londonSource note), researched via six parallel independent agent passes — one per district, not one broad sweep — each held to this file's existing Hard-rule-1 bar (verify who actually OWNS a venue, not just whether its name sounds unique; reject anything past 2-3 clustered sites; drop rather than guess when unsure). Prime Central London turned out to be the most ownership-group-saturated market this file has ever curated — most 'iconic' addresses belong to large restaurant/hospitality groups (Ivy Collection, Caprice Holdings, Corbin & King, D&D London, Birley Clubs, etc.) even when each site carries its own distinct name, so each research pass rejected roughly as many strong-looking candidates as it kept (see each district's own reasoning below). Every candidate's address was independently geocoded via postcodes.io (same real-postcode methodology as the rest of this file, not estimated), and every reason line was rewritten here for register consistency after the research pass. Landed at 32 venues across the 6 districts (Knightsbridge 5, Chelsea 6, Mayfair 5, Belgravia 6, Notting Hill 6, St James's 4) — an honest, uneven spread rather than a padded even one; both Knightsbridge and St James's have zero Drink venues after every hotel-bar/wine-merchant candidate found there failed the ownership check (see below), the same 'honest number, not a padded one' discipline already established elsewhere in this file (e.g. Cheadle Hulme/Prestbury). Three post-research corrections made during final review, tightening two of the six passes' own findings for consistency with the rest of this file's precedent rather than accepting them as-is: The Cow (Notting Hill) was dropped despite clean ownership — its real postcode (W2 5QH) sits outside Notting Hill's W11 bounds, the same 'wrong district is a real accuracy bug' standard the Santorini coordinate-correction pass already established, and Books for Cooks (Blenheim Crescent, unambiguous W11, zero ownership ambiguity) was promoted from the same research pass's own suggested alternate to replace it. Berry Bros & Rudd and the American Bar at The Stafford (both St James's) were dropped despite the research pass's own strong case for each — both were honestly flagged by that pass as borderline (Berry Bros has international trading offices and a Washington DC retail shop alongside its London flagship; the Stafford's sister hotel, Northcote, is ~250 miles away in Lancashire, a far larger spread than any 2-site pair this file has ever accepted, e.g. Lime Tree's Bollington sibling or Cibo's Cheshire-area siblings) — applying the same bar this file has held everywhere else (Isabel Mayfair, Zafferano and Juniper were all rejected on materially similar grounds) meant dropping both rather than carving out a one-off exception. Introduces 9 new venue types: LEBANESE RESTAURANT (Ishbilia) and BOTANICAL GARDEN (Chelsea Physic Garden) and COOKBOOK SHOP (Books for Cooks) are mapped onto existing tiles ('Neighbourhood favourite', 'Parks & green space', 'Cookery & craft' respectively) in src/lib/scoring/tile-catalog-map.ts; TURKISH RESTAURANT, BRITISH RESTAURANT, TRADITIONAL PUB, BOUTIQUE, INDEPENDENT BOOKSHOP and HISTORIC HOUSE are left category-only, same precedent as this file's many existing category-only types, since no existing tile fits any of them precisely. JAPANESE RESTAURANT (Chisou) and WINE BAR (Hedonism Wines, Sova) reuse types already introduced for earlier Manchester venues (Yuzu; The Wine Cellar and others) rather than introducing anything new. Real per-venue petFriendly/dietaryOptions researched for all 32 with this file's existing conservative-default rule (true/an option only where a source explicitly confirmed it, never inferred from venue type) — Medlar, Martino's, The March Hare, The Wee Sister and La Poule au Pot came back with confirmed dog-friendly signals; the rest defaulted to false/['none'] on a genuine no-signal-found basis, not a research gap.
_riyadhVenueSource: 2026-09-15, at explicit user request: first venues for Riyadh's 5 districts (see docs/data/districts.json's own _riyadhSource note), researched via five parallel independent agent passes — one per district. Saudi Arabia has a nationwide alcohol ban, so unlike every other market in this file, 'Drink' venues here are drawn entirely from the region-scoped catalog added for Riyadh's onboarding (specialty coffee, mocktail lounges, tea houses, shisha lounges, dessert cafés, juice bars, hotel lounges, rooftop cafés — see HomeRegion's own doc comment, src/types/models.ts); none of those 8 tiles had ever been wired to a real venue type before this pass (zero Riyadh venues existed), closed here alongside the venues themselves rather than left dangling. Riyadh's English-documented independent scene turned out thinner and far more chain-saturated than London's — most well-reviewed venues belong to regional or international hospitality groups (Beefbar, Allo Beirut, Almayass, Yauatcha, LPM, tashas Group, The Independent Food Company, tenant rosters at Via Riyadh and Boulevard City) even when Saudi-founded; several passes landed well under their target rather than pad the list, which is the honest, expected outcome given the rigor applied, not a research shortfall. Landed at 17 venues across the 5 districts (Olaya 5, KAFD 2, Diriyah 4, JAX District 5, Hittin 1) — an intentionally uneven, honest spread: KAFD and Hittin in particular are thin first passes (KAFD's real independent F&B scene is dominated by chains with a UK/international footprint even when Saudi-owned; Hittin's own district description turned out to overstate its real boundary, see districts.json's own _hittinBoundaryCorrectionSource note — most of what looked like Hittin venues actually sit in neighbouring Al-Hada/Al Nakheel and were correctly excluded). A small number of candidates the research passes themselves flagged as borderline were dropped on final review for consistency with how this file has treated the same pattern elsewhere: Apple Butter and A.O.K Kitchen (both KAFD) are UK-founded brands with a Riyadh outpost — the same international-footprint bar that excluded Isabel Mayfair/Zafferano/Juniper/Berry Bros & Rudd elsewhere in this file — dropped despite otherwise clean small-operator ownership. The Globe (Olaya, inside Al Faisaliah Tower) and The Vinyl Ember (KAFD, inside the Kimpton KAFD hotel) were kept despite sitting inside internationally-managed hotel towers: both are singular, distinctly-conceived venues with no replicated template elsewhere, the same 'one flagship, whoever owns the building' precedent Harrods Food Halls already established for London — this is a different pattern from a hotel chain's generic in-house lounge amenity (Bab Samhan, Marriott, correctly rejected by the Diriyah pass for exactly that reason). Coordinates: Saudi Arabia has no UK-style postcode system, so geocoding used Nominatim (OpenStreetMap's free geocoder, 1 req/sec rate-limited), same as the Santorini pass — several venues' specific buildings aren't yet mapped in OpenStreetMap (KAFD, JAX District and Bujairi Terrace are all very recent developments), so where a precise building-level geocode wasn't available, each venue was placed at its real, independently-confirmed district/complex anchor (Al Faisaliah Tower for Olaya's Faisaliah-adjacent venues; At-Turaif for Bujairi Terrace/Zallal; the JAX District and KAFD centroids already verified when those districts were first scaffolded; the Northern Ring Road point for Hittin) with a small manual spread so venues in the same complex don't stack on one exact pixel — an honest area-level approximation, not a fabricated precise address, the same standard the Santorini pass already established for this file. Chèrie's exact street (Olaya proper vs. the adjacent Tahlia corridor) came back genuinely ambiguous across sources; placed near its confirmed Al Faisaliah-adjacent anchor rather than guessed more precisely. Real per-venue petFriendly/dietaryOptions researched with this file's existing conservative-default rule — every Riyadh venue came back with no explicit confirming source for either, so all 17 default to false/['none'], an honest reflection of thin English-language coverage on this specific detail rather than a research gap. Introduces 6 new venue types: SHISHA LOUNGE, DESSERT CAFE and HOTEL LOUNGE map onto three of the real Riyadh Drink tiles (Shisha lounges, Dessert cafés, Hotel lounges respectively) in src/lib/scoring/tile-catalog-map.ts; COFFEE ROOM (already existing) is now also wired to 'Specialty coffee'. The remaining three Riyadh Drink tiles (Mocktail lounges, Tea houses, Juice & smoothie bars) still match zero venues — a real coverage gap for the next Riyadh pass, not wired to anything yet since inventing a mapping with no venue behind it would be premature. SAUDI HERITAGE CUISINE (TAKYA) and FIRE GRILL (Robata) are left category-only (Eat) — both are distinct enough from existing cuisine types (MIDDLE EASTERN in particular) to warrant their own label rather than a loose fit. CONTEMPORARY ART MUSEUM (SAMOCA) is left category-only (Do) — a purpose-built national museum is a different register from a commercial ART GALLERY. MIDDLE EASTERN and SPA (Aseeb, Base & Boon) and ART GALLERY and COFFEE ROOM reuse types already established elsewhere in this file.
_cheshireGolfClubsSource: 20 real Cheshire golf clubs added 2026-09-18 at explicit user request ('the 20 best, including dunham forest'), on top of the two already seeded (Wilmslow Golf Club, Prestbury Golf Club — neither re-added). Sourced from Today's Golfer's Cheshire Top 10, Golf Monthly, Top100GolfCourses.com, official club sites, Companies House and trade press; every address independently geocoded via postcodes.io. Frodsham Golf Club was an early candidate but is independently confirmed permanently closed (2022, site being converted to woodland by the Woodland Trust) — not included. Royal Liverpool, Wallasey and Stockport Golf Club all turn up in older 'Cheshire' rankings (golf directories often keep the pre-1974 county boundary) but sit in Wirral/Stockport under current local government — excluded as genuinely not Cheshire today. Each club assigned to its real nearest existing Curia district by distance (same 'real location over name' precedent as Wilmslow Golf Club/Mobberley), not a new one invented per club — every one of the 20 fell within a sensible distance of an existing district, several sharing one (Tarporley: Delamere Forest, Carden Park, Macdonald Portal; Prestbury: Mottram Hall, The Tytherington Club; Northwich: Sandiway, Vale Royal Abbey, Warrington GC; Nantwich: Wychwood Park, Malkins Bank, Crewe GC; Chester: Chester GC, Helsby GC; Altrincham: Dunham Forest, Lymm GC). Three have a genuine administrative wrinkle worth recording rather than hiding: Dunham Forest (Dunham Massey) has sat in the Metropolitan Borough of Trafford, Greater Manchester, since 1974; Warrington Golf Club and Lymm Golf Club both sit in the separate Warrington unitary authority, not Cheshire East/West. All three are within the historic/ceremonial county of Cheshire, read as Cheshire in real character, and are described as Cheshire clubs by golf publications and the clubs themselves — the same 'real historic-county-identity over the modern council line' judgment this file already made for Cheadle Hulme, Bramhall and Heaton Moor (all administratively Stockport, Greater Manchester) — not a new standard invented for golf. Ownership checked individually, not assumed: 15 of the 20 are genuinely independent single-site clubs. The other 5 are real group/chain cases, handled as ownership inputs to a distinctiveness score rather than exclusions, per the two-gate model — Fairmont Cheshire/The Mere (Accor, a large global hotel brand, following a 2026 Dubai-backed redevelopment; ownership='group'), Champneys Mottram Hall (Champneys Group, ~6 UK properties; ownership='small_group'), Macdonald Portal (Macdonald Hotels, 35+ UK hotels; ownership='group'), The Tytherington Club (The Club Company, ~17 UK clubs; ownership='group'), and Wychwood Park (single-asset, owned by Mokan Hotels and managed by Legacy Hotels — one property under outside management, not a chain footprint, so ownership='independent' with the management relationship noted). Carden Park is explicitly independent despite resort scale — 14 years under De Vere management ended in 2014, now fully independently owned by Steve Morgan CBE. Malkins Bank is council-owned and genuinely pay-and-play (Cheshire East Council, operated by R.M. Estates) — not a commercial chain of any kind, ownership='independent', scored at the lower, 'comfortable and accessible' end of distinctiveness on its own merits rather than excluded. Distinctiveness scored individually against real, specific facts (course architect, founding history, real character), not defaulted: Delamere Forest at 5 (the correction's own highest-rated Cheshire course, a real Herbert Fowler heathland original); Dunham Forest, Sandiway, Vale Royal Abbey, Carden Park, Chester GC, Helsby GC and Knutsford GC at 4 (each with a genuinely singular, sourced story — a WWII POW camp, an Open-qualifying test, a 16th-century abbey clubhouse, the first Nicklaus father/son design, one of the county's oldest clubs, a hilltop sandstone pedigree, a Lord Egerton private-course origin respectively); the remaining independents at 3 (good, real, well-run clubs without a standout singular claim); the four group/chain resorts at 3 (Fairmont/Carden's tier already covered above); Malkins Bank at 2 (competent and genuinely accessible, not aiming to be singular). distinctiveness/ownership/ownership_notes applied via supabase/migrations/0019_cheshire_golf_clubs.sql, not stored in this JSON — same convention as every venue added since migration 0009.
_tileCoverageGapSource: 2026-09-18, at explicit user report from the admin dashboard's tile-coverage stat ('22 of 54 tiles have zero matching real venues... we need to fix this'): checked all 17 real zero-coverage tiles (the admin count itself was also wrong — see src/lib/admin/admin-data.tsx's own fix note — 22 was computed against a stale, region-scoped venue snapshot; the real number against all 329 live venues was 17). Three were pure mapping gaps — real, live venues already existed but were never wired to their tile (see tile-catalog-map.ts's own comments): Culture (11 venues — museums, heritage centres, historic houses/churches), Clothes shopping (6 venues — fashion boutiques), Nightclubs (2 venues — Enigma Club, Koo Club). No new venues needed for those three. Three more were genuine density gaps with no existing venue type that fit, closed here with one real, individually-verified Manchester venue each: The Frog and Bucket (Comedy) — 102 Oldham Street, founded and still run by Dave Perkin since 1993/94, no second site found, ownership='independent', distinctiveness=4 (genuinely one of the most respected clubs of its kind in the UK, not just a local room). The Whiskey Jar (Whisky & spirits) — 14 Tariff Street, a two-floor Grade I-listed mill conversion, no second site found, ownership='independent', distinctiveness=4. Port Street Beer House (Beer gardens) — 39-41 Port Street, opened 2011 by Jonny and Charlotte Heyes; verified via Companies House and its own site that it's part of Common & Co (MCR) Ltd, a real 6-venue independent Manchester craft-beer group (Common, Port Street Beer House, The Beagle, The Pilcrow, Indy Man Beer Con, Summer Beer Thing) — genuinely local and characterful but a real enough footprint to warrant ownership='group' rather than stretching 'small_group' the way Cibo's 5-site case did; distinctiveness=4 regardless (CAMRA-listed, seven handpumps, a real destination garden). Coordinates for all three from postcodes.io geocodes of their own real addresses. Eleven tiles remain genuinely open, not done in this pass: Drink | Waterside bars, Wellness bars (UK) and Juice & smoothie bars, Rooftop cafés, Mocktail lounges (Riyadh — the latter two already flagged as known gaps in _riyadhVenueSourceSecondPass); Eat | Romantic, Business lunch, Chef's counter, Al fresco, Private dining, Wine-led dining — these six read as needing individual editorial judgment about which *existing* fine-dining-adjacent venues genuinely fit each mood (the same treatment 'Lively & loud'/'Neighbourhood favourite' already got in tile-catalog-map.ts), not a blanket type-wire or a single new venue each, and weren't rushed to fit this pass. distinctiveness/ownership/ownership_notes for the three new venues applied via supabase/migrations/0016_tile_coverage_gaps.sql, not stored in this JSON — same convention as every venue added since migration 0009.
_tarporleyNorthwichVenueSource: First venues for Tarporley and Northwich, 2026-09-18 — see districts.json's own _tarporleyNorthwichCorridorSource note for why these two districts exist at all (closing the real map gap between Chester/Nantwich and the main Manchester/Cheshire cluster). Deliberately seeded 3 venues each rather than this file's usual 'none yet' first-pass starting point, since MIN_MATCHES_TO_RANK in the redesigned Districts view (src/app/(tabs)/list.tsx, 2026-09-18) means a district needs 3 real matches to even appear there — the whole point of adding these two was for them to actually render, not sit invisible. Tarporley: Ginger and Pickles Bakehouse (51 High Street, CW6 0DP) confirmed via its own site to also run a Nantwich bakehouse — a real 2-site sibling pair, ownership='small_group'. The Swan (50 High Street, CW6 0AG), a genuine 16th-century coaching inn, owned by Si and Chrissie Lees Jones for 25+ years but day-to-day run by Cheshire operator Bear Inns — the ownership itself reads as independent (one long-tenured owning couple, a single specific historic identity), the management-company detail noted rather than hidden, ownership='independent'. The Hollies Farm Shop is seeded at its real address (Forest Road, Little Budworth, CW6 9ES, 3.5 miles from Tarporley's own centroid, comfortably inside the 5.5-mile coverage radius) rather than literally in Tarporley village — same precedent Wilmslow Golf Club/Mobberley already set (real location over name association); Cowap family-run since 1959, a second 'on the High Street' location mentioned in sourcing pushed this to ownership='small_group' rather than a flat independent. Northwich: Kanya Bistro Bar (36 High Street, CW9 5BE, trading since 2004, no second site found) ownership='independent'. The Salthouse NW (Hayhurst Quay, CW9 5HD) has a confirmed sister venue, The BullRing NW, both under the same family — ownership='small_group'. Barons Quay Social (Unit 5, Weaver Point Way, CW9 5FT), owner Carl Thomas, no second site found — ownership='independent'. All six pass Gate 1 cleanly (CLAUDE.md Hard rule 1) — real, specific, non-formula places, not high-street brands. Distinctiveness scored individually, not defaulted: The Swan/Salthouse NW/Barons Quay Social at 4 (a 400-year continuous identity, a genuine craft-ale specialism, and a rooftop-over-the-river format the town didn't have before, respectively); Ginger and Pickles at 4 (real scratch bakehouse, well-reviewed, not a generic village-bakery formula); The Hollies Farm Shop and Kanya Bistro Bar at 3 (both genuinely good and reliable, but a fairly common English farm-shop and modern-bistro format respectively, not singular). Dietary tags are a reasonable inference (vegetarian, given each venue's format), not individually confirmed the way Piccolino Grande/Cibo Gran Cafe's were — flagged rather than overstated as sourced fact. distinctiveness/ownership/ownership_notes values applied via supabase/migrations/0015_tarporley_northwich.sql, not stored in this JSON — same convention Piccolino Grande/Cibo Gran Cafe already set (see that note for why).
_riyadhVenueSourceSecondPass: 2026-09-15, at explicit user request ('i need more venues than just 17'): a second research pass per district, this time explicitly pushing Arabic-language sourcing (the first pass searched mostly in English; Riyadh's real independent scene is much better documented in Arabic, confirmed repeatedly this round) and telling each agent exactly what the first pass already found so nothing duplicated. Landed 9 more genuine, verified venues: Olaya +2 (Hewar Art Gallery, Lyrs Artisan Bakery), Diriyah +3 (HODAJ, Ghaymat Samhan, Saba Lounge), JAX District +3 (OffBrief, With Heart, Personage), Hittin +1 (Kasbah) — bringing the Riyadh total to 26 across the 5 districts. Several of these have a thinner verification trail than this file's usual bar (no named owner, verification resting on 'no evidence of a second site' rather than a positive ownership record) — flagged here rather than silently treated as equivalent to a fully-sourced entry, since Riyadh's smaller independents generally have much less English or even Arabic web presence than this file's UK venues did at the same stage. Woods Specialty Café (Olaya, at the 3-site cap and actively soliciting franchise partners on franchisecenter.sa) and Sharq (Diriyah, a 3-city restaurant with no identifiable small owner, reading as an organically-expanding chain rather than a sibling-pair) were both found and dropped for real chain-signal reasons; Avak (Hittin) and Petit Café (Hittin) were dropped on the same 'when unsure, drop' basis the whole project has held to — Avak's possible link to Aline Kamakian's multi-city Mayrig group couldn't be ruled out, and Petit Café's identical name to an established Beirut original (trademark-marked) plus a London outpost reads as an imported concept, not a single Riyadh operator. KAFD stayed at 2 venues despite a dedicated second pass: the only new leads found (Sira, Cloud 14, Riya Maison, Lafana, Kanza Pool Lounge) are all brand-new restaurants inside Atheel and W Riyadh, two hotels that had literally opened about a week before this research ran — real candidates for a future pass once they have actual independent verification (reviews, confirmed walk-in/public access) rather than just opening-announcement coverage, not included here since that would be publishing an unconfirmed lead as settled data. Introduces 2 new venue types: TEA HOUSE (HODAJ) is now wired to the real 'Tea houses' Riyadh Drink tile in src/lib/scoring/tile-catalog-map.ts, closing one of the three gaps the first pass left open; MOROCCAN LOUNGE (Kasbah) is left category-only (Drink) — distinct enough from every existing Drink type (not hotel-based, not a shisha-only concept) to warrant its own label. 'Mocktail lounges' and 'Juice & smoothie bars' still match zero venues — the two remaining real gaps for whenever the next Riyadh pass happens.
